major_event: Goldfinch Prime wind-down, full Prime investor redemption, contract pause, and transition of the legacy protocol to maintenance mode for borrower recoveries

duplicate_check.notes: No canonical Goldfinch match. Rejection is based on current CYA scope, not duplication.

notes: Phase 10 scope review confirms that Goldfinch is fundamentally a DeFi lending protocol rather than a CeFi lending/yield platform. Goldfinch governance GIP-87 and its July 7, 2026 follow-up establish an orderly Goldfinch Prime wind-down, full Prime investor redemption, contract pause, and legacy V1 recovery-only maintenance. Those facts are historically relevant but do not override CYA's fixed README scope, which focuses on CeFi lending/yield and explicitly does not prioritize DeFi lending protocols or pool-level records. Keeping Goldfinch in the active queue would repeatedly consume CeFi-growth research capacity and risk mixing protocol/pool outcomes with platform-level customer outcomes. This decision is scope-based, not an adverse assessment of Goldfinch, and may be revisited only if CYA formally expands its scope.

major_event: Current WeFi operates an onchain/deobank-style crypto platform with WFI cloud-based mining and loyalty/token rewards; the public site also markets up to 18% APR around stablecoins while separately stating that high-yield stablecoin savings and loans are coming soon

duplicate_check.notes: Exact CYA repository searches for WeFi, wefi.co and wefi.xyz returned no canonical identity match before this scope decision. The Issue #186 discovery identity resolves to the current wefi.co ecosystem promoted in Japanese high-yield/mining material, not the separate legacy WeFi Finance lending protocol at wefi.xyz.

notes: Phase 10 identity/scope review resolves the watchlist item to the current WeFi ecosystem at wefi.co. First-party material describes Cloud-Based Mining as hardware-free WFI token distribution/reward infrastructure and the current platform as exchange, payments, custody, cards and token/loyalty infrastructure. The June 1, 2026 Terms state that WeFi is not a bank, does not accept deposits on a banking balance sheet, and does not use user funds for lending or credit creation. The public site uses yield/APR language and shows 'up to 18% APR' around stablecoins, but the same current surface explicitly labels high-yield stablecoin savings up to 18% and loans as 'coming soon'; reviewed sources therefore do not establish a live CeFi interest/savings product with durable deposit, return, redemption and counterparty mechanics. CYA's fixed scope focuses on CeFi lending and yield platforms and does not treat token mining/distribution by itself as a yield-platform record. The separate wefi.xyz identity is a DeFi lending/leverage protocol and is also outside the initial CeFi-focused scope. Do not create a canonical CYA platform from either identity under this watchlist item. Re-review wefi.co if a live stablecoin savings/interest product launches with first-party terms and product mechanics.

major_event: Current Luxera/XERA DAO ecosystem combines blockchain payments and token staking; first-party material describes the XERA protocol as non-custodial and explicitly refers to stakers and node operators, while current user-facing guides show active wallet-connected XERA staking with fixed lock periods

duplicate_check.notes: Exact CYA repository searches for Luxera, XERA DAO, xeradao.com, xera.pro, Xera Global and cya_candidate_000114 returned no canonical or staging match before this decision. The current Luxera/XERA DAO identity at xeradao.com is kept distinct from the older ASIC/Moneysmart alert identity Xera/Xera Global at xera.pro and web.xera.pro.

notes: Phase 10 identity review resolves the Issue #186 XERA watchlist item to the current Luxera/XERA DAO ecosystem at xeradao.com. First-party about material describes XERA primarily as a DAO token/payment ecosystem and states that the protocol is non-custodial, that no one can access or control stakers' funds, and that independent node operators participate in the protocol. Current user-facing material confirms active wallet-connected XERA staking and lock periods, but those referral guides and third-party Luxera promotional sites are discovery/support evidence and must not establish canonical return rates or safety claims. Under CYA's fixed initial scope, generic non-custodial token staking without a verified major suspension, customer-outcome, failure, or regulatory event is not prioritized and should not consume a canonical platform ID. This is a scope decision only, not a fraud, safety, solvency or return-quality classification. A separate ASIC/Moneysmart investor-alert entry exists for Xera/Xera Global at xera.pro and web.xera.pro, added in April 2024; that older identity predates and is not evidence against the current xeradao.com Luxera identity, so the two must not be conflated. Re-review Luxera/XERA DAO only if CYA expands its scope or if first-party/regulatory evidence establishes a material staking freeze, access/outcome event, shutdown, or other historically significant change. Advertised staking rates remain issuer/promoter claims and are not verified realized yield.

duplicate_check.notes: Exact CYA repository searches for Crypto DAO, cryptodao.pro, cryptodao.club and cya_candidate_000115 returned no canonical or staging match before this decision. The current cryptodao.pro identity is not the unrelated legacy cryptodao.com exchange listing/history.

notes: Phase 10 identity/scope review resolves the watchlist CDAO item to the current Crypto DAO at cryptodao.pro, with a live companion interface at cryptodao.club and a public repository self-described as the official Crypto DAO documentation repository. The live interface exposes staking, sub-token staking, bonds, DAO rewards, governance and swap functions and links referral activity back to cryptodao.pro. The project's StakingPool smart contract implements on-chain stake/unstake and rebase mechanics around token contracts and a reward manager, supporting classification as a DeFi/on-chain staking protocol rather than a centralized interest account. Current user-facing guides describe PRO staking, fixed lock periods, auto-compounding/rebase earnings, vesting and referral mechanics, but those guides are discovery/support evidence and must not establish canonical rates or realized returns. No verified major shutdown, staking freeze, customer-loss/outcome process, or regulator action tied to the current cryptodao.pro identity was found in this first pass. Under CYA's fixed initial scope, generic DeFi/rebase token staking without a historically significant suspension/outcome/failure event is not prioritized and should not consume a canonical platform ID. This is a scope decision only, not a fraud, safety, solvency or sustainability classification. Re-review if CYA expands into generic DeFi staking or if authoritative evidence establishes a material withdrawal/staking restriction, protocol failure, regulator action or customer-outcome event. Any advertised APR/APY or theoretical compounding result remains an issuer/promoter claim, not verified realized yield.

major_event: Current CryptoPawn is a borrower-side crypto-collateralized cash-loan service operated by BitHills Inc.; customers pledge crypto assets as collateral and receive Japanese-yen loans, while staking rewards, airdrops and similar economic rights arising from collateral belong to BitHills unless it chooses to pass some or all of them to the borrower

duplicate_check.notes: Exact CYA repository searches for CryptoPawn and cya_candidate_000117 returned no existing identity match before staging. The Issue #186 target resolves to the Japanese cryptopawn.io service operated by BitHills Inc.; it is distinct from the separate US cryptopawn.com / CryptoPawn, Inc. pawn-lending identity.

notes: Phase 10 identity/scope review resolves the watchlist CryptoPawn item to cryptopawn.io, operated by BitHills Inc. First-party company, FAQ and service pages consistently describe a borrower-side product: a customer pledges BTC, ETH, USDT and other crypto assets as collateral, receives a cash/Japanese-yen loan, pays borrowing interest and receives the collateral back after repayment. The FAQ states that staking rewards, airdrops, hard-fork rights and other economic value arising from pledged collateral belong to BitHills during the custody period, with any pass-through to the customer left to BitHills' discretion. That clause does not establish a public depositor interest/yield account; it is part of the collateral-loan economics. CYA's fixed initial scope is a CeFi lending/yield archive centered on customer-side yield/interest products and historically significant access/outcome events, not a general catalog of crypto-backed borrowing services. No separate public lender/investor yield product tied to the cryptopawn.io identity was found in the reviewed first-party material. Accordingly this identity is out of current CYA scope. This is a scope decision only and is not a safety, solvency, licensing, tax or return-quality assessment. Do not import claims from the separate cryptopawn.com identity into this record. Re-review only if BitHills launches a public crypto interest/lending product for depositors or if CYA formally expands to borrower-side crypto-backed lending.
